title: GPU Performance of an Entropy-Stable Discontinuous Galerkin Euler Solver with Non-Conservative Terms
summary: The entropy-stable discontinuous Galerkin method for compressible Euler equations with buoyancy is implemented on graphics processing unit (GPU) hardware. We measure the performance of the solver on three-dimensional problems: the rising thermal bubble and the baroclinic instability in a channel. On NVIDIA A100 hardware, the solver achieves nearly 70\% of 64-bit floating-point peak performance for the most computationally expensive kernel (volume terms) and significantly reduces the computational overhead typically incurred by two point entropy-stable fluxes in the volume terms.
